requirement: The book preprocessor MUST escape requirement names and link targets when inserting badge HTML. It MUST encode badge label and message text in Shields.io URL path components so punctuation cannot change the badge URL structure.
rationale:
I found no gaps. The requirement has three obligations, and the code and tests cover each.

**1. Escape requirement names when inserting badge HTML.**
- `src/lib.rs#fn[replace_definitions]` computes `escaped_name = escape_html(&full_name)` and uses it in the badge `id`. It also escapes the anchor in the term `<strong id>`.
- `src/lib.rs#fn[escape_html]` replaces `& < > " '` with HTML entities.
- `src/lib.rs#fn[shield_badge]` escapes the label and message in the `alt` text and the URL in `src`. This function is reached from both marked `{impl}` items, so it needs no marker of its own.
- Valid names contain no HTML-special characters, so the escaping in `replace_definitions` cannot be exercised through that path. It is a direct call to `escape_html`. `escape_html` is tested through `shield_badge` in `badge_urls_percent_encode_punctuation_and_html_is_escaped`, which asserts that `<`, `>`, `&`, `"` and `'` in the `alt` text become entities.

**2. Escape link targets when inserting badge HTML.**
- `src/lib.rs#fn[reference_badge]` wraps the `chapter_href` result in `escape_html`. It does the same for the built-in title text.
- `replace_definitions` escapes `detail_href` the same way.
- `reference_link_targets_are_escaped` runs `preprocess_book` on a chapter whose rendered path contains `& " < >`. It asserts that the `href` is entity-escaped and that no raw `"q"` or `<x>` appears in the output.
- The `detail_href` escaping in `replace_definitions` has no test of its own. It is a plain call to `escape_html`, which the tests above exercise.

**3. Encode badge label and message text in Shields.io URL path components.**
- `src/lib.rs#fn[shield_path_component]` percent-encodes every byte except `A–Z a–z 0–9 .`. It maps a space to `_`, `_` to `__` and `-` to `--`. `shield_badge` applies it to both the label and the message.
- `badge_urls_percent_encode_punctuation_and_html_is_escaped` asserts the exact URL for `/ ? # % & < > " '` and non-ASCII input.
- `shields_badge_urls_escape_requirement_names` asserts the `_` and `-` doubling and the space-to-underscore mapping.

Other callers of `shield_badge` (`replace_query_directives` and the index detail rendering) get the same encoding through the shared function.

text: The book preprocessor MUST escape requirement names and link targets when inserting badge HTML. It MUST encode badge label and message text in Shields.io URL path components so punctuation cannot change the badge URL structure.
